saints.name: St. Etheldreda
saints.title: Abbess
saints.shortBlurb: An East Anglian princess who kept her vow of virginity through two marriages and founded the abbey of Ely…
biography: Born in 636 at Exning in Suffolk, a daughter of Anna, king of the East Angles, Etheldreda, Audrey in later English, was given about 652 to Tondberht, prince of the South Gyrwe, from whom she received the Isle of Ely as her morning gift. She kept her vow of virginity through that marriage and, after Tondberht's death, through a second in 660 to the boy Ecgfrith of Northumbria.

When Ecgfrith came to the throne she begged leave for the cloister, and about 672, with the counsel of Bishop Wilfrid, entered the double monastery of Coldingham under the king's aunt Ebba. Fleeing thence to her own isle, she founded at Ely in 673 a monastery for monks and nuns and ruled it as abbess in great austerity.

She died on 23 June 679 of a tumour of the neck, which she called a just repayment for the necklaces she had loved as a girl; Bede composed a hymn in her praise. Sixteen years later her sister Sexburga, her successor, found the body incorrupt. The lace of her Ely fair lives on in the word 'tawdry,' a corruption of Audrey.
saints.knownFor: Founding Ely Abbey; her consecrated virginity.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 23 June
